source.title: A boy with Prader-Willi syndrome: unmasking precocious puberty during growth hormone replacement therapy.

confirmation.summary: Holm and Cassidy clinical score 9; methylation-specific PCR showed only the methylated maternal allele.
evidence: the genetic test demonstrated only the methylated maternal allele, thus confirming the clinical diagnosis of PWS by the methylation-specific PCR

note.text: At birth our son was very floppy, both testicles had not come down, and he sucked weakly and gained little weight in the first month. He kept growing poorly as a baby. Around age two he started eating all the time and put on weight quickly. By six he was shorter than nearly all boys his age and carried a lot of body fat. His hands and feet are small, his knees angle inward, and he has some mild trouble with learning.
note.author: Peter's Kiro, written from the article's findings; not the parent's words
